games.title: Kriegsspiel
games.note: In 1824 Prussia's king ordered every army regiment to receive a set, making it the first wargame adopted for officer training.

games.title: Little Wars
games.note: Novelist H. G. Wells wrote these rules for toy-soldier battles, with an appendix comparing them to Kriegsspiel.

games.title: Monopoly
games.note: Grew out of Lizzie Magie's 1904 The Landlord's Game, which she designed to show the harm of land monopolies.

games.title: Pentominoes
games.note: Mathematician Solomon Golomb named these twelve shapes, each made of five joined squares, in 1953.

games.title: Braunstein
games.note: A refereed Napoleonic wargame where players ran individual townspeople of a fictional German town instead of armies.

games.title: Chainmail
games.note: Its 14-page fantasy supplement added heroes, wizards, elves and dragons to medieval miniatures battles.

games.title: Dungeons & Dragons
games.note: The first 1974 set still told players to use Chainmail's miniatures rules to settle combat.

games.title: Traveller
games.note: One of the first science fiction tabletop role-playing games.

games.title: Civilization (board game)
games.note: Published by Hartland Trefoil in Britain, then by Avalon Hill in the US in 1981. MicroProse later licensed the name.

games.title: Empire (1973)
games.note: A PLATO starship battle game written as coursework by Iowa State student John Daleske; possibly the first networked multiplayer action game.

games.title: Netrek
games.note: A team-based online space battle game that players kept running over the internet for decades.

games.title: Spasim
games.note: A 32-player networked 3D space flight game on the PLATO system, released in March 1974.

games.title: dnd
games.note: Also called The Game of Dungeons; often credited as the first game with what players now call a boss.

games.title: pedit5
games.note: PLATO administrators kept deleting it as a waste of computer time, and its creator kept restoring it.

games.title: Moria (1975)
games.note: A PLATO dungeon game where up to ten players explored together in first-person wireframe 3D.

games.title: Oubliette
games.note: Began as a tool to roll dice for Dungeons & Dragons games, then grew into a multiplayer PLATO dungeon crawl.

games.title: Avatar (1979)
games.dev: Bruce Maggs, Andrew Shapira & David Sides
games.note: Accounted for 6% of all hours spent on PLATO between 1978 and 1985, by Richard Bartle's count.

games.title: Wizardry: Proving Grounds of the Mad Overlord
games.note: Players build a party of six and map a ten-floor dungeon seen in first person.

games.title: Telengard
games.note: Daniel Lawrence's home computer version of DND, a dungeon game he had first written for a mainframe.

games.title: The Bard's Tale
games.note: Sold about 407,000 copies, the best-selling computer RPG of the 1980s by one count.

games.title: Wasteland
games.note: Electronic Arts kept the Wasteland name, so Interplay's spiritual successor came out as Fallout.

games.title: The Portopia Serial Murder Case
games.note: Hideo Kojima has named it one of the three most influential games he has played.

games.title: The Tower of Druaga
games.note: Players climb 60 floors, each hiding a treasure that only appears after an obscure action.

games.title: Dragon Slayer
games.note: Nihon Falcom's early action RPG for Japanese home computers; its series later included Xanadu.

games.title: Hydlide
games.note: The hero recovers health by standing still, a mechanic Ys later borrowed.

games.title: Ys I: Ancient Ys Vanished
games.note: Combat works by running into enemies slightly off-center, a fast 'bump' system.

links.took: The idea of a rules-based war game, which Wells and Jerome K. Jerome adapted for toys.
